title: My Helper, God, I Bless His Name
description: My Helper, God, I Bless His Name in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 889 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My help-er, God, I bless his name; The same his power, his grace the same; The to-kens of his friend-ly care O-pen, and crown, and close, the year.

lines: My helper, God, I bless his name;
The same his power, his grace the same;
The tokens of his friendly care
Open, and crown, and close, the year.
And see, when I survey my ways,
Thus far his arm hath led me on;
Thus far I make his mercy known;
And, while I tread this mortal land,
New mercies shall new songs demand.

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
